insight.title: The Statistician Who Armored the Undamaged Parts of Planes
insight.subtitle: How a counterintuitive decision during WWII saved thousands of pilots.
insight.notificationHook: He armored the parts without bullet holes

sections.text: During World War II, the military wanted to armor returning bombers. They analyzed the bullet holes on surviving aircraft, planning to reinforce the most heavily damaged areas.
But statistician Abraham Wald disagreed. He ordered the mechanics to armor the completely untouched areas instead, defying the obvious data presented right in front of them.
Wald realized the surviving planes only showed where a bomber could be hit and still fly. The planes hit in the clean areas had all crashed at sea.
The most critical lessons are often hidden in what didn't happen.

news.title: UK, Poland set to sign defence treaty to tackle hostile threats across Europe
news.description: LONDON, May 26 - Britain will sign a new defence and security treaty with Poland on Wednesday to strengthen defence cooperation in the face of increasing hostile threats across Europe, the government said, following similar deals with France and Germany.

news.context: The United Kingdom and Poland are preparing to sign a bilateral security pact to counter European threats.
news.next: Other European nations may form similar bilateral defense pacts to bypass bureaucratic delays.
news.bigger: European security structures are shifting toward decentralized, regional alliances rather than relying solely on NATO.

news.title: Iran medicine shortages worsened by war
news.description: Amid a fragile ceasefire with the US and Israel, Iranians are finding it harder to access essential medicines as imports and payment systems are disrupted.
news.why: Iranian patients may struggle to access lifesaving treatments and prescription drugs.
news.context: Ongoing conflict and financial sanctions have disrupted import pipelines, causing a shortage of critical drugs in Iran.

news.why: Financial institutions may operate with heavily armed security forces on-site.
news.context: Russia enacted legislation authorizing major banks and financial entities to deploy military defense systems against drone threats.
news.next: Commercial banks in Russia could begin installing private anti-drone jamming networks.
news.bigger: Private corporate security is increasingly blending with national military operations in conflict zones.

news.context: The CDC called for internal volunteers to scale up health screening operations at American international airports.
